newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JACKSON SENDS WARNING TO JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JACKSON SENDS WARNING TO JOHNSON.

text.p: Britain's world record holder Colin Jackson warned American Allen Johnson on Wednesday that he has a battle on his hands to defend his world 110 metres hurdles title.

Jackson, with much to prove after injury forced him to concede his world title to Johnson in 1995 and lack of form deprived him of an Olympic medal in Atlanta last year, beat the American into second place with a controlled, flowing performance in the semifinals.
The Welshman won in 13.24 seconds with Johnson second in 13.31. Slovak Igor Kovac and American Terry Reese took the other places in Thursday's final from the heat.
In the second semifinal Jackson's team mate Tony Jarrett, the silver medallist in 1995, failed to make the final after a tight finish. Jarrett finished sixth.
Despite his victory, Jackson, who set the world record of 12.91 on his way to gold at the 1993 championships in Stuttgart, said he felt like an underdog for the first time for many years.
"There is no pressure. For the first time in five years people are not really looking at me," Jackson said. "It is a great feeling. I just want to show that Colin Jackson is still around."
Johnson is not looking as formidable as he did at last year's Olympics when he won gold and Jackson finished fourth,

"It was hard, so hard," Johnson said. "I got on the blocks and felt drained. Every hurdle was a struggle. But the defeat to Colin has not affected me psychologically. All I wanted to do was finish in the top two and get a good lane for the final. I'll be ready."
A handful of runners dipped for the line together in the second semifinal.

Just one tenth of a second separated the quartet who went through to the final -- Germany's Olympic bronze medallist Florian Schwarthoff (13.29), France's Dan Philibert (13.30), American Mark Crear (13.35) and Pole Artur Kohutek (13.39).
